Order 
The present petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner seeking quashment of FIR bearing crime No. 346/2014 registered at Police Station Kotwali District Datia for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120 of IPC as well as all subsequent proceedings arising out of the said FIR.

2. As per prosecution case, the complainant filed a complaint alleging that his grandmother, Smt.
Patiya Kushwah, resided with him throughout her lifetime and died on 09.05.2014 after illness,
whereupon her last rites were performed by him.

During her lifetime, she executed a registered Will dated 26.09.1997 before the Sub-Registrar, Datia, bequeathing all her movable and immovable properties in favour of the complainant's three sons-- Mulchandra Kushwah, Mahendra Kushwah and Ranu Kushwah--with NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4513 2 MCRC-9644-2014 accused Narayan Kushwah as a witness.
The complainant possesses all her original identity and property documents.

When the complainant approached Halka Patwari Chandrashekhar Shrivastava for mutation on the basis of the Will, the Patwari dishonestly demanded a bribe of Rs.1,00,000/- to mutate the land situated at village Jhadia, failing which he threatened mutation by inheritance.

Subsequently, upon notice of mutation proceedings filed by the complainant, the Patwari conspired with accused Narayan Kushwah and Advocate Badam Kushwah to prepare a Badam Singh Kushwah vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136415876/

sentences.text: 1 forged Will in favour of Narayan Kushwah, which was notarized by Notary Advocate Rakesh Chaubey using a photograph taken from the deceased's condolence pamphlet and false attesting witnesses.

Further, the Patwari prepared forged applications, Panchanama, and fabricated seals and signatures of a Ward Councillor who was in jail at the relevant time, and caused the same to be filed ante-dated before the Tehsildar.
On the basis of these forged documents, Narayan Kushwah obtained an illegal mutation order dated 16.06.2014.

Thus, all accused persons, in furtherance of their common intention, committed cheating, forgery, fabrication of documents, and fraud with the object of illegally usurping the land of the complainant's grandmother.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the sole allegation against the present petitioner is that he merely identified Smt. Patiya Bai.
It is pertinent to mention that the land in question originally belonged to the first husband of Smt. Patiya Bai.
After the death of her first husband, she remarried; however, she succeeded to the land left by her first husband in accordance with law.

It is further submitted that Smt. Patiya Bai executed an NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4513 3 MCRC-9644-2014 earlier Will in favour of the nephew of her second husband, wherein the land situated at Village Jhadiya was specifically excluded.
Subsequently, she executed a second Will in respect of the land situated at Village Jhadiya in favour of the nephew of her first husband.
Thus, the land in question indisputably pertains to the estate of the first husband of Smt. Patiya Bai.

Ignoring all these material and admitted facts, the impugned F.I.R. has been mechanically registered against the petitioner, without any allegation of active participation,
dishonest intention, or criminal conspiracy.
4. It is submitted that in the present case the FIR was registered on 28.09.2014, and till date, even after the lapse of more than eleven years, the chargesheet has not been filed.
The investigation in a criminal case is intrinsically linked with the fundamental right to speedy trial guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

Prolonged and unexplained delay in investigation, by itself,
constitutes a grave violation of this valuable right and strikes at the very root of the criminal proceedings, rendering them liable to be quashed.
The accused cannot be subjected to an indefinite state of uncertainty, anxiety, and mental agony on account of a never-ending investigation and the looming threat of trial proceedings.
Thus, on this ground alone, the impugned FIR deserves to be quashed.

In support of this submission, learned counsel for the petitioner places reliance upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Robert Lalchungnunga Chongthu @ R.L. Chongthu v.
State of Bihar, reported in 2025 SCC OnLine SC 2511.
5.

It is an admitted position that even after lapse of more than eleven years from the date of registration of the FIR, the investigating agency has not filed any charge- sheet.

Apart from this bald assertion, nothing is placed on record to demonstrate any concrete steps taken by the investigating agency during this long period or any genuine impediment which prevented completion of investigation.

8. Investigation in a criminal case is an integral facet of the right to speedy trial, which forms an essential component of the right to life and personal liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
An accused person cannot be subjected to perpetual uncertainty and anxiety on account of a never-ending investigation.
The sword of a possible prosecution cannot be allowed to hang over the head of an individual indefinitely.

9. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Robert Lalchungnunga Chongthu @ R.L. Chongthu v. State of Bihar, 2025 SCC OnLine SC 2511 , has reiterated that investigation is squarely covered under the umbrella of the right to speedy trial.

entities.text: Robert Lalchungnunga Chongthu @ R.L. Chongthu v. State of Bihar, 2025 SCC OnLine SC 2511
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been held that violation of this right can strike at the very root of the investigation itself, leading to its quashment.

The Supreme Court NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4513 5 MCRC-9644-2014 has further observed that although no rigid timeline can be prescribed for completion of investigation, Article 21 would undoubtedly be impacted where no justification, much less a reasonable one, can be discerned from the record for the inordinate delay in completing the investigation.
The accused cannot be made to suffer endlessly with the threat of continuing investigation and eventual trial proceedings bearing upon their everyday existence.

10. Applying the aforesaid principles to the present case, this Court finds that the record does not disclose any justification, much less a reasonable one, for the investigating agency having taken more than a decade to complete the investigation.
Why the investigation in the present matter has remained pending for such an extraordinarily long period is not explained.
No reason is forthcoming either in the case diary or from the submissions of the State which can rationally account for this prolonged inaction.

The petitioner has, therefore, had the cloud of a criminal investigation hanging over his head for more than eleven years, which by itself constitutes a grave infraction of his fundamental right under Article 21.
11.

Without entering into the merits of the allegations or the rival claims relating to the validity of the Wills or ownership of the property, this Court is of the view that continuation of the criminal proceedings in the face of such unexplained and inordinate delay would amount to abuse of the process of law.
12. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

FIR bearing Crime No.346/2014 registered at Police Station Kotwali, District Datia, for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4513 6 MCRC-9644-2014 Indian Penal Code and all consequential proceedings arising therefrom insofar as it relate to present petitioner are hereby quashed.
No order as to costs.
